epic.title: Email migration: sixteen addresses, 1,736 accounts, the old domain's quiet year
epic.description:
Move Phil's mail off philipwhelan.com onto sixteen purpose addresses at IONOS (eight on philwhelan.com, eight on sporebit.com), with one mailbox, a folder per address and only phil@ and vault@ notifying; secure every High account in the census on the way (address, password, 2FA, Proton Pass); recover IONOS, Proton and Microsoft through Gmail only; put SPF, DKIM and DMARC on all three domains, monitor then enforce; let everything else change as its mail arrives through the old domain's catch-all; and give the old domain a quiet year from the day the last High account moves, with a month-eleven review. Mail and DNS stay at IONOS, and nothing extra is spent unless Phil decides it on a ticket.

## Order
mail.01 (IONOS limits) and mail.02 (Proton limit) first. mail.03 imports the census; mail.04 remaps its High rows. mail.05 builds the address plan (history moved, old mailboxes retired, the sixteen made), then mail.06 (folders and notifications), mail.07 (catch-all), mail.08 (recovery anchor) and mail.09 (SPF and DKIM, then DMARC monitoring). mail.15 writes the per-account routine. The critical accounts go next, each its own ticket: mail.16 Microsoft, mail.17 Apple, mail.18 banks, mail.19 HMRC and pension, mail.20 hosting, mail.21 Mercedes, mail.22 eBay (before FixForward), mail.23 AI accounts. mail.14's watched dry run comes before mail.24's High batches, which are generated from the import. mail.26 makes the old-domain counter. Alongside: mail.10 enforce, mail.11 non-sending domains (after keys.11), mail.12 inbox@, mail.13 app sending, mail.25 shop aliases (if mail.02 says pay), mail.27 Gmail unsubscribe, mail.28 legacy addresses, mail.29 Proton Pass clean-up, mail.30 fixclothing.co.uk, mail.31 DropShipAuto, mail.32 public trail, mail.33 calendars and files, mail.36 plain-text passwords, mail.37 Proton hardening, mail.38 and mail.39 (assumed items). Then mail.34 refusers, mail.35 the quiet year starts, mail.40 closing report, mail.41 done check.

## Done means
The old mailboxes are closed (mail.41), every High row in the census is moved, closed or recorded as refused with a choice, the closing report is in Docs, and the month-eleven review ticket exists.

## Flags
- `[claude]` section 1 answer 16: a lapsed domain can be bought and receive reset emails. Not reopened; the quiet year and the month-eleven review stand.
- `[claude]` H1.6: an alias per shop reverses section 1 answer 8 and may cost money against answer 7 ("nothing extra"). Not reopened; mail.02 checks the plan and the limit first.
- `[claude]` H2.4: the broadband decision links to SEC answer 18; it touches this epic only through the renewals look-up (IONOS Mail Basic, philipwhelan.com and the Sporebit domains' dates in fin.14). Not reopened.

## Dossier
The research dossier (`dossiers/mail.md`, checked 2026-11-28) is attached in Docs: LINK

tickets.title: Check the IONOS Mail Basic mailbox and forward limits against the sixteen-address plan
tickets.description:
## What
Claude prepares a one-page finding on the epic; Phil signs in to IONOS and reads four numbers off the Email & Office page. The finding answers: which Mail Basic variant the contract is (Mail Basic 1, 1+ or 5), how many mailboxes it holds and how many are in use, the size of every existing mailbox (pw@ and philip@ on philipwhelan.com, the May and October mailboxes, both catch@), and whether forwarding addresses are unlimited on this contract. IONOS UK lists "Unlimited Forwarding addresses" on Mail Basic 5 (5 mailboxes, 2 GB each) and Mail Basic 1+ (1 mailbox, 12 GB) as of 2026-11-28. It also records two limits the dossier found: forwarding addresses cannot send, and IONOS only sends from an address on the same domain as the mailbox.

## Why
H1.2: one mailbox with a folder per address and the others as forwards; "first ticket checks the IONOS Mail Basic mailbox and forward limits". Section 1 answer 9 ("move it all across") needs the storage to fit.

## Done looks like
A comment on this ticket with: the variant, mailboxes total and in use, each mailbox's size, total history size against the kept mailbox's storage, the forwarding limit, and a yes or no on "can the kept mailbox send as a same-domain forward". If storage does not fit, the cost of 12 GB is written down and nothing is bought.

## Unlocks
mail.05 (the address plan can be built), mail.06 (the mailbox and forward shape).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Cost
Mail Basic today: about £1 to £5 a month excluding VAT depending on variant (IONOS UK, 2026-11-28). Extra storage or a mailbox is to be priced if needed. Nothing is bought in this run.

## Done looks like
A comment with the plan name, the alias count, the GBP price seen, and Phil's one-line decision (pay or shop@ direct). mail.25 is unblocked or closed to match.

The table uses the 0111 owner-only policy shape; the migration goes through `supabase db push` per AGENTS.md. The workbook itself is copied once into the nightly backup as a frozen source and is never edited again. No password, recovery code or Proton Pass secret is imported: only names, addresses and flags.

H1.10: the inventory is imported into Mycelium, owner-only, and becomes the checklist's data (state in the database); the workbook is kept frozen in the nightly backup.

Row counts in the table match the workbook (3,198 total, 1,736 account-type). Kirsty's session sees zero rows (isolation test). The frozen workbook is in the next nightly backup. A comment on this ticket gives the migration number and commit.

tickets.title: Recovery anchor: IONOS, Proton and the Microsoft account recover through Gmail only; vault@ for everything else

Every other account uses vault@philwhelan.com for recovery, and vault@ is never used for these three.

## Why
H1.4: the IONOS account, Proton and the Microsoft account log in or recover through Gmail only, never through an address on a domain IONOS hosts.

## Done looks like
Each of the three shows Gmail as its recovery email and no IONOS-hosted address. The guide's answer box says yes.

## Unlocks
mail.16 (Microsoft clean-up), mail.17 (Apple), mail.20 (IONOS and hosting), and every account ticket that sets vault@ as recovery.

## Depends on

Claude lists every calendar on Phil's Google account: the eight May sub-calendars (Personal, Birthdays, Events, Family/Household Admin, Finance, Fitness, Sporebit, Travel), Family and Phirsty Life, plus any others found. For each: which app or agent writes to it (the old VPS agent, Mycelium, PhirstMaxx, by hand), who it is shared with (Kirsty, family) and the last event date. The output is a keep-or-merge checklist for one sitting of Phil's.

## Why
H2.9 (assumed): one ticket lists every calendar, what writes to it and who sees it, for a keep-or-merge sitting.

## Done looks like
A comment with the table; a short keep-or-merge checklist is ready for Phil.

## Unlocks
A keep-or-merge sitting; mail.33 (calendars on old-address accounts).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## What
After the quiet year has started, Claude writes the closing report from the census: accounts moved, closed, refused and reopened, 2FA kinds, sittings spent, what is left changing as mail arrives, and the month-eleven date. It is saved to Docs and summarised in one line on the Day log.

## Why
Section 1b: a closing report (accounts moved, closed, secured, effort) saved to Docs and the Day log.

## Done looks like
The report exists in Docs with its link on this ticket; the Day log has the line.

## Unlocks
mail.41 (the done check).

## Depends on
mail.35: the quiet year has started.

## What
One live check: no mailbox remains on philipwhelan.com except the catch-all, pw@ and philip@ history sits in phil@ under old folders, a test to pw@philipwhelan.com reaches the catch-all, and the last four weeks of the old-domain count are recorded.

## Why
Section 1 answer 27: done means old mailboxes closed.

## Done looks like
The guide's four steps are ticked with the counts filled in.

## Unlocks
The month-eleven review has its evidence.

## Depends on
mail.40: the closing report.

intro.answer: Confirm every mailbox on philipwhelan.com is closed and its history is in phil@, with only the catch-all left until the domain decision.

steps.title: List the mailboxes left on philipwhelan.com

where.label: IONOS > Menu > Email & Office

steps.body_html: Filter Email & Office by philipwhelan.com and list what remains.

steps.title: Check pw@ and philip@ history is in phil@

where.label: IONOS Webmail

steps.expect_html: phil@ has old/pw and old/philip folders with their message counts.
steps.body_html: In Webmail, open the old folders and compare their counts with mail.05's and mail.28's answers.

steps.title: Send a test to pw@philipwhelan.com

where.label: Gmail on the web

steps.expect_html: It lands in phil@ under old domain through the catch-all.
steps.body_html: From Gmail, send one message to pw@philipwhelan.com.

steps.title: Read the weekly count

where.label: Mycelium > the mail import checklist (this epic)

steps.expect_html: The daily line's old-domain count for the last four weeks is written below.
steps.body_html: Open the daily line's old-domain counter and type the last four weekly numbers.
